corrected_value.authors: Román-González, M., Pérez-González, J. C., & Jiménez-Fernández, C.
corrected_value.title: Which cognitive abilities underlie computational thinking? Criterion validity of the computational thinking test.

decisions.quote:
The current project investigated the influence of cognitive skills on CT in students from
Grades 7 and 8: First, we wanted to replicate the contribution of reasoning, spatial abilities
and numerical abilities by assessing the same subskills as Román-González et al. (2017).
decisions.reason: The shipped row misidentified the replicated original as Román-González et al. (2018, Computers in Human Behavior, 80, DOI: 10.1016/j.chb.2017.09.030), which is cited only once in passing as corroborating background in the Discussion (line 780). Throughout the Abstract ('Román-González et al. (Computers in Human Behaviour 72)'), Introduction, Method, and Discussion, the study explicitly replicates Román-González, Pérez-González, & Jiménez-Fernández (2017, Computers in Human Behavior, 72, 678-691, DOI: 10.1016/j.chb.2016.08.047), matching blind target 0.

decisions.quote:
Concerning the replication part of our project, our results support the view that CT is
underpinned by reasoning, as assessed by figural reasoning, and spatial abilities, as
assessed by visualization. However, in contrast to the original study, we also found
a significant association between CT and mental arithmetic.
decisions.reason: For the resolved original study (Román-González et al., 2017), the replication tested the contributions of figural reasoning, visualization, and mental arithmetic to computational thinking (CT), as well as gender differences. While the authors replicated the positive associations and unique regression contributions of figural reasoning and visualization (and higher male CTt scores, though not fully explained by cognitive skills), they explicitly mark the mental arithmetic result as diverging from the original null finding ('However, in contrast to the original study, we also found a significant association between CT and mental arithmetic' and 'Our observation of a small positive association between mental arithmetic and CT does not replicate previous findings by Román-González et al. (2017)'). Under the codebook, confirming part of the tested findings while explicitly contrasting another tested finding as not replicating yields a 'mixed' outcome.

decisions.quote:
The current project investigated the influence of cognitive skills on CT in students from
Grades 7 and 8: First, we wanted to replicate the contribution of reasoning, spatial abilities

decisions.reason: The study collected new data from a sample of 132 Austrian students in Grades 7 and 8 to re-test the published findings of Román-González et al. (2017), making it a replication.
